summary:
Shell part of brief 2 built and verified.
- O-R1 overview routing (I1): no link opens a California overview with no default fire and no build. closeIncident(), missingIncidentId (an unknown or old link falls back to the overview with a notice), and history: explicit opens push, Back returns to the overview, Forward reopens, '← All fires' goes back or closes. A named fire loads in parallel with the three CAL FIRE lists (live, the 2026 season via year=2026, 2025 via year=2025; bbox_lonlat typed; I2 web side).
- Decision 10 (zoom focus): useStore.focusIncidentFromMap(id|null), debounced 300 ms, prepared fires only. It never builds, frames or pushes history. The time defaults to the latest observation and Play then animates the spread from the start. incidentSource is set atomically with incidentId; the last 4 fires are cached for instant re-focus; selection, preset, perspective, basemap and view survive. Verified end to end with the map's viewport logic.
- O-R3: overview panel (Active / 2026 season / 2025 filters, CAL FIRE official rows, honest loading, error and empty states, phone peek sheet '7 active fires · CAL FIRE, updated hh:mm', the California 'Official now' block). Header: 'California · all fires' or '← All fires' plus the picker, one 'Public · Command · Forensic' switch.
- O-R6: fire card (I3) with CAL FIRE's official record and link, 'Analysis ready' or 'Prepare analysis (1-3 min)' (the only path that builds), Play spread, Check a location, Open in 3D.
- O-R7: Forensic opens map-first: timeline-only dock and a labelled 'Frame fire' on desktop, a collapsed sheet on phones, a cyan 3D selection pin, click-to-select. With no fire it says 'Zoom in on a fire or pick one'.
- O-R10: Public defaults to aerial and Command to dark. A user pick wins; the map's fallback never counts as a pick; the URL writes basemap only when it differs from the preset's default.
- C-R9: --m-text-3 #98a4b2 and more opaque Public panels. Every measured text is now at least 6.3:1 on dark, aerial and roads (text-3 measured 3.4-4.6:1 in the audit). The research note and credits sit on opaque chips; meta is 12 px. The default Public view keeps 75.7-77.5 % open map on all 10 bundles.
- C-R2 (phones): one-line strip, note and '© Credits' on one line, a compact timeline, cards capped at 42vh, a clicked pin panned above the sheet.
- U-R4: labelled phone 'Updates' button with the official badge; OfficialNow mounted; the satellite chip mounted (header bar from 1024 px).
- U-R9: Command data status gains Cal OES, NWS and CAL FIRE rows, and a past fire's CAL FIRE row now shows the year and 'Last edit of CAL FIRE's record'. Public gets one freshness line. Desktop Public opens on a compact 'Official now' summary to keep the 75 % map share; Details shows the full block, data rows and feed.
verification:
Gates (final run):
- web typecheck (tsc -b): 0 errors.
- lint: 55 warnings, all in src/scene (the baseline); 0 elsewhere; SelectionPin adds none.
- vitest: 55 files / 671 tests pass, including 11 new or extended test files: overview, catalog, history, store (fetch stub: 404 fallback, explicit-only builds, closeIncident drops late answers, year=2026/2025 list requests, focus vs open, the debounce, unprepared ids ignored, latest-observation time, cache reuse with no file refetch, LRU of 4), workspace (basemap rules, URL rule, fire card, view rule, returnToIncident -> frameFire, MapFlyTo.source), views and strip form, build rules, pointHidden, officialSummary, dataStatus official rows and freshness, api client query.
- build: ok; three.js stays out of the main chunk (0 WebGLRenderer).
- backend: uv run pytest -q 597 passed.

In the app (API 8712 with FIRE3D_LIVE=0, Vite 5182, Playwright Chrome; scripts in the session scratchpad b2s/):
- flow.mjs (history): overview -> card -> 'Open this fire' (push, len 3, fromOverview) -> Back (overview) -> Forward (Henderson) -> 'All fires' (history.back) -> deep link Eaton -> 'All fires' (push) -> Back (Eaton). An unknown link lands on the overview with the notice and a replaced URL (incident and t dropped). 0 build POSTs, 0 errors.
- zoomfocus.mjs (decision 10, with the map's own viewport logic): zoom in on Henderson focuses it (source zoom, time = latest observation, URL replaced, history length unchanged, header, panel and timeline switch); zoom out returns to the overview; zooming in again uses the cache (0 bundle requests); Play restarts at the window start.
- fxclick.mjs (Forensic): a drag does not select, a click on the terrain selects (34.1916, -118.1013), and the map card shows it.
- keys2.mjs: the fire list is one tab stop with arrows; Enter opens the card and focuses its heading; Escape closes it and returns focus (to the focused fire's 'Official now' heading when the list gave way).
- coverage2.mjs (waits for framing 'done' + 7 s): Public default at 1440x900 is 75.7-77.5 % on all 10 bundles (Eaton 75.7, Palisades 75.7, Madre 76.3, Lidia 76.3, Camino 76.4, Cooley 76.2, Henderson 76.2, Norte 75.9, fixture-demo 77.5, fixture-live 77.1). Command is 60.5-62.0 %. Phones at 390x844 are 59.1-60.7 % (the audit had 53.4 %).
- contrast.mjs (computed colours; every translucent layer composited over the real basemap pixels behind the text; minimum of the mean, p90 and p10 pixels; Eaton z14 with a card):
  - Public minimum per basemap: dark 6.63, aerial 6.77, roads 6.30 (text-3 card eyebrow); search placeholder 6.50-6.77.
  - Command: data status labels 6.74-7.35, feed meta 7.52, official block meta 9.79-10.27.
  - Overview: list sub-lines 8.58-9.60, fire card meta 8.86-9.76.
  - Research note 9.82 and credits 10.02 on every basemap (opaque chips).
  - The audit had text-3 at 3.38-4.62.
- Forensic before/after: before docs/screenshots/redesign-final-1440-forensic.png (brief 1), after brief2-shell-forensic-1440.png. Only the dock (timeline only), the labelled Frame fire / Charts & key events and the view switch labels changed; with a point the pin shows (forensic-pin-1440). The console shows only the pre-existing THREE.Clock deprecation.
- finals.mjs: 26 screenshots at 1440x900, 1024x768 and 390x844, all viewed; 0 build POSTs, 0 page errors.
- Count-only secret scan of the touched files and scripts: 0 files contain the FIRMS key.
contract_deviations: I5 'Shell mounts OfficialNow at the top of UpdatesPanel': on desktop Public the panel opens on a compact 'Official now' (ui/shell/officialSummary.ts). It shows three short lines built from the same useOfficialNow() data, with verbatim zone status and NWS event, issuer and distance, quiet states saying 'Not an all-clear', a data-freshness line and the standing line. 'Details' in the panel header expands to OfficialNow, the data rows and the feed. Command, the phone sheet and the expanded panel always mount OfficialNow at the top. Reason: OfficialNow is 380-780 px tall, and with it the default Public view fell to 64-68 % open map (target 75 %).

I5 ImageryChip 'floating data-chrome element next to the map controls': from 1024 px it sits in the header bar, right above the map controls (the bar is chrome anyway, so it costs no map area). Below 1024 px it uses the .mw-imagery slot next to the controls (phones: its own row, hidden while a card or sheet is open).
CONTRACT §2 edited outside §13 (basemap field comments and the URL rule), as the O-R10 item asks ('Update CONTRACT §2').

store.autoBuild (the Forensic setting 'Auto-build unbuilt incidents') now defaults to false and only feeds the incident picker. selectIncident's autoBuild option is an explicit request, no longer gated by the setting. A 404 now returns to the overview (missingIncidentId) instead of an error banner with a useless Retry.

selectIncident gained an optional `source` (IncidentSource) and closeIncident sets incidentSource null; MapFlyTo gained an optional `source: 'official'` (for official-web's fitOfficialBounds; the map side is not wired yet).
The overview's list uses the updates slot and its open flag (panels.updates); there are no incident updates without a fire.
Phones: the map credits fold behind a labelled '© Credits' toggle on the note's line (the same pattern as MapLibre's compact attribution); the full credits open above the bottom row.
known_issues: The 75 % margin is thin: the lowest bundles (Eaton, Palisades) measure 75.7 %. It depends on other components' heights (the legend's rows, the archived NWS line, the credits length). A taller official summary line or another legend row could push them under 75 %.
Phones with a point selected: location's four-block card (up to about 670 px of content) is capped at 42vh and scrolls; about 170 px of map stays visible above it (the audit had 100-150 px).
Command's default view is 60.5-62.0 % open map (brief 1: 62.5-66.0 %), because the full OfficialNow block and the data status share its panel; Command is denser by design and has no 75 % target.

Other owners' meta text stays at 11 px: the timeline's status line (.ctl uses --m-fs-xs) and the legend labels. Raising --m-fs-xs to 12 px globally wraps the legend to 5 rows (Henderson 74.5 %), so I kept 11 px and documented the token roles.

Zoom-focus candidates come from the three loaded lists. A prepared past fire under the 2025 list's threshold (300 ac, or 100 with the picker's switch) would not be focusable; today all 8 prepared real fires are listed. The fixtures are not in any list.
'← All fires' on a zoom-focused fire pushes an overview entry, so Back then reopens that fire explicitly (framed). This is consistent with replace-on-zoom, but it may surprise.

Clicking a prepared fire's row flies to it, and the map's zoom focus then opens it, so the overview list gives way to the fire's updates panel (focus moves to its 'Official now' heading). This is intended by decision 10.
The main start-up chunk is 435 kB (brief 1: 300 kB): new official, location and shell modules. three.js stays out.
Pre-existing: Forensic logs the THREE.Clock deprecation; the map's pin label can run past the right edge on phones (map's).
